analysis.themes: A Puritan family exiled to the wilderness turns on itself — faith, guilt, and adolescent awakening make the supernatural almost secondary to the family's own fear.
analysis.atmosphere: Oppressive dread built from grey skies, candlelight, and scripture; the horror feels earned and ancient rather than manufactured.
analysis.narrative: Slow-burn escalation as each family member's piety becomes a vector for suspicion, culminating in collapse and dark liberation.
analysis.visual: Natural-light cinematography and desaturated tones give 1630s New England a documentary bleakness.
analysis.characters: Thomasin's arc from scapegoated daughter to self-possession is the film's dark spine; the parents embody faith curdled into paranoia.
